title: House and Hymn
premise: Orsen Kavanagh, a hospice nurse who has spent her life perfecting the art of not being noticed, takes a night post at Marrow House, where the dying patients all count backwards in their sleep—and the house's old recording equipment captures something answering them. As Orsen digs into the recordings, she realizes the second voice is learning names, and that her own name has begun appearing in the counts. The found family of staff and patients she never meant to care about becomes the thing she must save: the voice feeds on being remembered, and it has chosen Marrow House's residents as its next chorus. In the end, Orsen does the one thing she swore she'd never do—makes herself unforgettable—offering the voice her own memories as ransom, and walks out with the family intact but carrying a count of her own that will someday reach zero.
about_author: K. M. Vasquez is a former night-shift caregiver who writes horror about the quiet hours when institutions breathe. They live in a drafty farmhouse with two cats and an unexplained habit of counting stairs.

chapters.title: The Night Intake
chapters.summary: Orsen arrives at Marrow House, determined to remain invisible among the staff and terminal residents. She notices patients murmuring numbers in their sleep but files it away as coincidence. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: guarded detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Counts and Cassettes
chapters.summary: Night aide Dev points out that every dying patient counts backwards from different starting numbers—and always reaches zero within a week of death. Orsen finds a reel-to-reel recorder in the basement, still running, tapes labeled by decade. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Playing the oldest tape, Orsen hears a patient counting and a low, patient voice answering questions no one asked aloud. The voice asks about names. Orsen tells herself it's bleed-through from another recording. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: denial straining against evidence.

chapters.title: Mrs. Adeyemi Counts to Nine
chapters.summary: Resident Mrs. Adeyemi begins counting from nine; meanwhile she starts telling Orsen intimate things about her childhood that Orsen never shared. The staff grow closer around the dying woman, and Orsen, against her rules, lets herself be included. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Digging through archives, Orsen learns Marrow House was once a sanatorium where a nurse recorded the dying to 'preserve their last words'—and that staff vanished whenever the counts accelerated. Dev admits he's heard his own name on the tapes. POV: alternating Orsen and Dev. Emotional beat: dread becoming shared burden.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Mrs. Adeyemi reaches zero and dies peacefully—but that night every resident begins counting at once, staggered like a round song. The voice on the new recording says Orsen's full name, correctly, twice. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: terror fused with fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Orsen tries to get the residents transferred; administration stonewalls, and the voice punishes interference—a day nurse leaves mid-shift, memory frayed, unable to recall her children's faces. Orsen understands the stakes: it eats remembering itself. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: desperation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Chorus of Names
chapters.summary: The counts synchronize. Residents wake reciting names of the dead sanatorium staff, and the voice grows clearer, almost warm, promising belonging to anyone who answers it. Dev nearly does. Orsen pulls him back by telling him, for the first time, why she learned to be invisible. POV: Orsen and Dev. Emotional beat: found family forged under threat.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Climax. Orsen descends to the recorder room with the final tape and offers a trade: her memories, her name, her whole remembered self, in exchange for the residents' silence. The voice accepts—and Orsen discovers the count attached to her own life has already begun. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: sacrifice without heroics, fear and love entangled.

chapters.title: Hymn for the Unforgotten
chapters.summary: The house goes quiet; the residents stop counting, and the surviving staff bury the tapes together in the garden, a small ritual that feels like the family Orsen never planned to join. She stays on—not hidden anymore, though some mornings she can't recall her mother's face, and sometimes, softly, she counts. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging, earned at cost.
